title: Compare fractions
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

sections.title: Same-size pieces
sections.objective: Compare fractions with the same denominator by comparing the tops.
explain: When two fractions have the same bottom, the pieces are the same size. {5/8} is 5 eighths and {3/8} is 3 eighths.
So just compare how many pieces: 5 is more than 3, so {5/8} > {3/8}.
The open side of the sign faces the bigger amount: {3/8} < {5/8} says the same thing.

sections.title: Compare to one half and one
sections.objective: Decide whether a fraction is more or less than {1/2} or 1, and which of 0, {1/2}, 1 it is closest to.
explain: One half of the bottom number is the halfway point. For {3/7}: half of 7 is 3½, and 3 is less than that, so {3/7} < {1/2}.
Don't compare only the tops. {2/7} has a bigger top than {1/2}, but 2 sevenths is less than half of the bar.
A fraction equals 1 when the top equals the bottom ({7/7} = 1). If the top is bigger, it's more than 1: {9/7} > 1.
Closest to 0, {1/2} or 1? Compare the top with 0, half the bottom, and the whole bottom. {7/8}: 7 is right next to 8, so it's closest to 1.

sections.title: Different-size pieces
sections.objective: Compare fractions with different denominators by rewriting them with a common denominator.
explain: A bigger bottom means smaller pieces. {3/5} > {3/8}: both are 3 pieces, but fifths are bigger than eighths.
When the tops and the bottoms are different, rewrite both over a common denominator, then compare the tops. {3/4} = {9/12} and {5/6} = {10/12}, so {3/4} < {5/6}.
Careful: {3/4} and {5/6} are each missing one piece, but they aren't equal. A missing sixth is smaller than a missing fourth, so {5/6} is closer to 1.

visual.caption: Cut both bars into the same number of pieces. Then you can see which shading is longer.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Compare fractions of every kind, mixed together.
explain: Now the problems are mixed. Pick the quickest way for each one.
Same bottoms: compare the tops. Same tops: the smaller bottom is bigger. Otherwise: think about {1/2} and 1, or rewrite over a common denominator.

hints.frac.compare.like: The pieces are the same size. Which fraction has more pieces?
hints.frac.compare.benchmark: Find half of the bottom number. Is the top more or less than that? For 1, compare the top with the bottom.
hints.frac.compare.unlike: Rewrite both fractions over a common denominator, then compare the tops.
hints.frac.compare: Same bottoms: compare the tops. Otherwise rewrite both over a common denominator, or compare each one to {1/2} or 1.

misconceptionMessages.frac.cmp-numerators-only: Comparing only the tops doesn't work when the pieces are different sizes. Compare each fraction with one half: is the top more or less than half the bottom?
misconceptionMessages.frac.cmp-bigger-denominator-bigger: A bigger bottom number means the whole is cut into more pieces, so each piece is smaller. Think about which pieces are bigger.
misconceptionMessages.frac.cmp-gap-equal: Both are missing pieces, but the missing pieces aren't the same size. Rewrite both over a common denominator to compare them.
